claims.text: A registry stores images by name (repository) and tag; docker pull downloads an image from a registry into the local image store, docker push uploads an image from the local store to a registry.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker image pull, docker image push; Get started > What is a registry?

claims.text: Image reference [HOST[:PORT]/]NAMESPACE/REPOSITORY[:TAG]: HOST names the registry; omitted -> Docker Hub (docker.io), and omitted namespace -> library (Docker Official Images), so caddy:2.10.0 = docker.io/library/caddy:2.10.0.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker image tag (Description: image reference components)

claims.text: docker pull caddy:2.10.0 (Docker 28.0.1) ends with the line docker.io/library/caddy:2.10.0; docker pull donhang-api:stage-1 fails: pull access denied for donhang-api, repository does not exist or may require 'docker login'.
claims.source_hint: executed on the author's machine, Docker 28.0.1, 2026-10-02

claims.text: mcr.microsoft.com is Microsoft's container registry, from which the .NET SDK and ASP.NET Core runtime images are pulled.

Dockerfile@stage-1 line 5 FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build, line 19 FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0; lab/Dockerfile@stage-1 line 3 FROM lscr.io/linuxserver/openssh-server:version-10.3_p1-r1.

docker-compose.yml@stage-1: web and app-web use image caddy:2.10.0 and db uses postgres:17.6-alpine with no build:, so they come from Docker Hub; api (lines 82-86) has build: context . dockerfile DonHang.Api/Dockerfile and image donhang-api:stage-1.
When a Dockerfile's FROM image is not in the local image store, docker build pulls it from its registry before building.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Dockerfile reference FROM; docker buildx build (--pull)

claims.text: With the default docker build driver (Docker Desktop's default builder), docker build loads the result into the local image store and uploads it to no registry unless asked (docker push, or --push).
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker buildx build (--load/--push), Build drivers: docker driver

claims.text: docker run uses the image in the local image store and pulls only when it is missing (default --pull=missing).
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker container run --pull (default missing)

claims.text: A registry stores and serves images; it does not run containers. Containers run on the host whose Docker engine started them (docker ps lists that host's containers).
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Docker overview (Docker architecture: client, daemon, registries)

claims.text: No file at stage-1 pushes donhang-api: no docker push in scripts/ or .github/workflows/ci.yml at stage-1; scripts/up.sh@stage-1 line 14 runs docker compose up -d --build --wait, so each machine builds its own copy.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: git grep 'docker push' stage-1; scripts/up.sh:14

claims.text: Each GitHub-hosted runner is a fresh machine discarded after its job (self-hosted runners are not); a job's image is gone with it unless a step saves it as an artifact (docker save + upload) or pushes it to a registry.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: About GitHub-hosted runners (each job gets a fresh VM)

claims.text: docker image ls donhang-api lists the locally built image with tag stage-1 after the stage-1 lab was built with scripts/up.sh.
claims.source_hint: executed: docker image ls on the author's machine (donhang-api:stage-1 de99f26f6ec6)

claims.text: docker save writes an image to a tar file and docker load reads it back into another machine's local image store, so an image can move between machines without a registry (as ci.yml@stage-2 does with images.tar).
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker image save, docker image load

claims.text: In the pull error 'pull access denied for donhang-api, repository does not exist', 'repository' means the image name (repository) on the registry, not a Git repository.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker image tag (NAMESPACE/REPOSITORY component)

claims.text: A registry accepts a push under a name that points at it: a name starting with its host (e.g. ghcr.io/...), or for Docker Hub a namespace/repository name with no host; the pusher needs write access there.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker image push; Get started: Build, tag, and publish an image (docker push my-username/my-image)
